key_insight: Reserving idle buffer qubits between users’ circuits offers a practical defense against crosstalk attacks during quantum multi-programming.
engineering_relevance: The method adds crosstalk-aware circuit allocation to OQTOPUS, open-source software already used to operate real quantum computers.
method: Characterize attack-induced energy relaxation and dephasing on a real quantum device.
Extend OQTOPUS allocation to reserve idle buffer qubits around circuits.
Verify that the allocator correctly reserves the buffer qubits.
evidence_signal: Real-device experiments found observable degradation in the dephasing characteristics of qubits adjacent to the attacker circuit; allocation checks confirmed correct buffer reservation.
watch_item: Buffer qubits consume chip capacity, and the abstract does not quantify their attack-mitigation benefit or throughput cost.
paper_title: Buffer-Qubit-Based Quantum Circuit Allocation Method Against Crosstalk Attacks
